reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify potential spurious features through pattern recognition in the input data, with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and validate shared attribution across misclassified instances. This ensures both contextual insight and numerical validation of spurious correlations that may not be immediately apparent through inspection alone.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (73, 291, 205) and evaluate their values for consistency across instances.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that appear in all three instances with their value ranges and potential spuriousness indicators

autonomous_tasks.query: Assess whether any shared feature (e.g., mean compactness or mean concavity) exhibits values that are statistically or semantically out of alignment with known cancer classification patterns in the dataset.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justification for why a shared feature might be spurious—such as being correlated with label due to noise, data leakage, or domain-specific bias

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides global feature importance with a game-theoretic foundation, helping identify features with high shared attribution across misclassifications. LIME offers local interpretability to confirm how individual features influence predictions. Integrated Gradients offer smooth, baseline-aware attribution, useful for detecting spurious patterns. Sensitivity analysis quantifies feature impact by removing them, isolating any shared feature that drives misclassification despite lacking semantic relevance.
